```{r uni_set_up, eval=T, include=FALSE}
   o1        =  r_o*cos(pi_vals)     # x-coordinates of objects

}
draw_starts = function(N = 1)
{
	r_x      =  runif(N,0,0.25)
	pi_x     =  runif(N,-1,1)*pi
	xt       =  matrix(cbind(r_x*cos(pi_x),r_x*sin(pi_x)),nrow = N,byrow = TRUE)
}

{
  plot(objects[,2]~objects[,1],type = 'n', ylim = c(-1,1), xlim = c(-1,1))

  x_edge = cos(pi_v)
  lines(y_edge~x_edge)
  lines(c(0.25*y_edge)~c(0.25*x_edge),lty = 2)
}
```

```{r,param_set_up,echo=T,}
set.seed(2024)

game_status = function(xt, objects, rad, center = matrix(c(0,0), nrow=1, ncol=2), outer_rad = 1)
{
  J        = nrow(objects)
  ones     = matrix(1, J, 1)
  dists    = sqrt(rowSums((objects - ones %*% xt)^2)) # distance btwn drone and ALL obj
  min_dist = min(dists) # dist to closest tree

  outer_circle_point_dist = sqrt(sum((center - xt)^2)) # distance between circle center and drone

  if (min_dist < rad) {
    status = -1                      # hit a tree/obj
  } else if (outer_circle_point_dist > outer_rad) {
    status = 1                       # escaped
  } else {
    status = 0                       # keep going
  }

  list(status = status, closest = objects[which.min(dists), , drop = FALSE], min_dist = min_dist)
}
```

```{r,game_exp_1,echo=T}
set.seed(2024)

draw_starts = function(N = 1)
{
	r_x      =  runif(N,0,0.25)
	pi_x     =  runif(N,-1,1)*pi
	xt       =  matrix(cbind(r_x*cos(pi_x),r_x*sin(pi_x)),nrow = N,byrow = TRUE)
	return(xt)
}

p     = 2
q     = 2
nodes =c(3,3)
npars = p*nodes[1]+nodes[1]*nodes[2]*+nodes[2]*q+nodes[1]+nodes[2]+q # total num param
theta_rand = runif(npars,-1,1)

#####################NN MOdel##############################

model = function(xt, theta, nodes = c(3,3))
{
  # Infer dimensions:
  N = dim(xt)[1]   
  p = dim(xt)[2]   # number of input features/coords
  q = 2            # output steps
  dims = c(p, nodes, q)   # p -> 3 -> 3 -> 2

  # Populate weight matrices:
  index = 1:(dims[1]*dims[2])
  W1    = matrix(theta[index], dims[1], dims[2])
  index = max(index) + 1:(dims[2]*dims[3])
  W2    = matrix(theta[index], dims[2], dims[3])
  index = max(index) + 1:(dims[3]*dims[4])
  W3    = matrix(theta[index], dims[3], dims[4])

  # Populate bias vectors:
  index = max(index) + 1:dims[2]
  b1    = matrix(theta[index], dims[2], 1)
  index = max(index) + 1:dims[3]
  b2    = matrix(theta[index], dims[3], 1)
  index = max(index) + 1:dims[4]
  b3    = matrix(theta[index], dims[4], 1)

  ones = matrix(1, N, 1)
  a0   = t(xt)

  # Evaluate the updating equation in matrix form
  a1 = tanh(t(W1) %*% a0 + b1 %*% t(ones))   # hidden layer 1
  a2_hidd = tanh(t(W2) %*% a1 + b2 %*% t(ones))   # hidden layer 2
  a3 = tanh(t(W3) %*% a2_hidd + b3 %*% t(ones))   # output layer

  # Return a list of relevant objects:
  return(list(a2 = matrix(a3, ncol = 2, nrow = 1)))
}



#################### plot game function
plot_game = function(xt,objects,rad,center=matrix(c(0,0),nrow=1,ncol=2),inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
{
  plot(NULL, type ='n', col = 'darkgreen',xlim=c(-2,2),ylim=c(-2,2))
       
  # plot inner and outer circles
  
  theta = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)

  x_inner = center[1] + inner_rad * cos(theta)
  y_inner = center[2] + inner_rad * sin(theta)


  x_outer = center[1] + outer_rad * cos(theta)
  y_outer = center[2] + outer_rad * sin(theta)

  
  lines(x_outer, y_outer, col = "purple", lwd = 2)
  lines(x_inner, y_inner, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  abline(h = 0, v = 0, col = "gray", lty = 2)
  
  points(xt[,2]~xt[,1],pch = 9,col = 'black')
  points(objects[,1],objects[,2],pch=19,col='darkgreen')
  abline(v = c(-1,1), lty = 3,col = 'black',lwd = 2)
  abline(h = c(-1,1), lty = 3,col = c('black','black'), lwd = 2)
}


####################################### game_play

# play a single game

play_a_game = function(xt,delt,objects,rad,theta,plt = F,trace = TRUE,nodes,inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
{
  k           =   1  # Count how many iterations
  xt          =   xt # Set the initial coordinate(s) for the drone.
  trajectory = matrix(0,2,100) # store the the postions that the drone takes through out the game/how it moves
  trajectory[,1] = t(x0)

  # Check the game status:
  res_status  = game_status(xt,objects,rad)

  if(plt)
  {
  	  plot_game(xt,objects,rad,center=matrix(c(0,0),nrow=1,ncol=2),inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
  }
  while((res_status$status==0)&(k<100)) # single game=100 steps
  {
    k = k+1
    
    # Now, let the model update the position of the pieces:
    ct = model(xt,theta,nodes)$a2 #res_status$closest
    xt =  xt+ct*delt
    
    #print(paste0('k: ',k,'xt_new: ',xt))

    # Checkk the game status after the positions are updates:
    
    res_status  = game_status(xt,objects,rad)
    
    trajectory[,k] = t(xt)
 
  }
  trajectory = trajectory[,1:k,drop = FALSE]
    if(plt)
  {
  	lines(trajectory[2,]~trajectory[1,],col = 'darkgrey')
  }
  
  dmin_final=sqrt(sum((res_status$closest - xt)^2))
  
  return(list(k = k, status = res_status$status,xt= xt,trajectory = trajectory,dmin=dmin_final))
}

#play_a_game(draw_starts(1),delt,objects,rad,theta_rand,nodes=c(3,3),plt = F)



############# Obj func
play_T_games = function(theta) # This is our obj function!
{
  inner_rad_in=0.25;outer_rad_in=1;T_games=100;J=50
  
	 # num trees/objects to avoid
  score=0
	for(i in 1:T_games)
	{
  objects =  objects # keeo constant for now
 #starting position
    xt_try=draw_starts(1)
    #apply across x_try
   res_play =play_a_game(xt_try,delt,objects,rad,theta,plt = FALSE,trace = FALSE,nodes=c(3,3),inner_rad=inner_rad_in,outer_rad=outer_rad_in)$status
   score  = score+(res_play==+1) # number of times when we got to the other side
	}
  return(score/T_games) # objective to maximise
}
```

**iii) Key Observations:**

-   The drone has a near perfect success rate at escaping the forest and the learned weights have learnt how to get around a specific configuration of forest across starting positions

-   However, with a new configuration of trees, the drones success rate plummets to 0, indicating that the initial model/weights were highly overfit for a specific distributions of tress across the field. Apart from hitting the objects, most of the drone's trajectories do not make it out of the outer circle in the given number of iteration steps (100). The model has not learnt a general pattern of how to escape the field (across object configurations).

#### c) Experimental Setup 2

**i)**

```{r,mod_nn,echo=T,eval=T}


model_2 = function(xt_input, theta, nodes = c(3,3),add_arg) #add_arg= 1/(dmin-r)
{
  xt=cbind(xt_input,add_arg)
  # Infer dimensions:
  N = dim(xt)[1]   
  p = dim(xt)[2]   # number of input features/coords
  q = 2            # output steps
  dims = c(p, nodes, q)   # p -> 3 -> 3 -> 2

  # Populate weight matrices:
  index = 1:(dims[1]*dims[2])
  W1    = matrix(theta[index], dims[1], dims[2])
  index = max(index) + 1:(dims[2]*dims[3])
  W2    = matrix(theta[index], dims[2], dims[3])
  index = max(index) + 1:(dims[3]*dims[4])
  W3    = matrix(theta[index], dims[3], dims[4])

  # Populate bias vectors:
  index = max(index) + 1:dims[2]
  b1    = matrix(theta[index], dims[2], 1)
  index = max(index) + 1:dims[3]
  b2    = matrix(theta[index], dims[3], 1)
  index = max(index) + 1:dims[4]
  b3    = matrix(theta[index], dims[4], 1)

  ones = matrix(1, N, 1)
  a0   = t(xt)

  # Evaluate the updating equation in matrix form
  a1 = tanh(t(W1) %*% a0 + b1 %*% t(ones))   # hidden layer 1
  a2_hidd = tanh(t(W2) %*% a1 + b2 %*% t(ones))   # hidden layer 2
  a3 = tanh(t(W3) %*% a2_hidd + b3 %*% t(ones))   # output layer

  # Return a list of relevant objects:
  return(list(a2 = matrix(a3, ncol = 2, nrow = 1)))
}


# Modify play_a_game function
# now includes d_min

play_a_game_mod = function(xt,delt,objects,rad,theta,plt = F,trace = TRUE,nodes=c(3,3),inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
{
  k           =   1  # Count how many iterations
  xt          =   xt # Set the initial coordinate(s) for the drone.
  trajectory = matrix(0,2,100) # store the the postions that the drone takes through out the game/how it moves
  trajectory[,1] = t(xt)

  # Check the game status:
  res_status  = game_status(xt,objects,rad)
  d_min=sqrt(sum((res_status$closest - xt)^2))
  
  if(plt)
  {
  	  plot_game(xt,objects,rad,center=matrix(c(0,0),nrow=1,ncol=2),inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
  }
  while((res_status$status==0)&(k<100)) # single game=100 steps
  {
    k = k+1
    
    # Now, let the model update the position of the pieces:
    add_arg=(1/(d_min-rad))
    ct = model_2(xt,theta,nodes,add_arg)$a2 #res_status$closest
    xt =  xt+ct*delt
    
    #print(paste0('k: ',k,'xt_new: ',xt))

    # Checkk the game status after the positions are updates:
    
    res_status  = game_status(xt,objects,rad)
    
    trajectory[,k] = t(xt)
 
  }
  trajectory = trajectory[,1:k,drop = FALSE]
    if(plt)
  {
  	lines(trajectory[2,]~trajectory[1,],col = 'darkred',lwd=2)
    #point(trajectory[2,]~trajectory[1,],col = 'darkred',lwd=2)  
    points(xt[,2]~xt[,1],pch = 9,col = 'black')
  }
  
  dmin_final=sqrt(sum((res_status$closest - xt)^2))
  
  return(list(k = k, status = res_status$status,xt= xt,trajectory = trajectory,dmin_final=dmin_final))
}
```

The model has an improved success rate of 17% for a new configuration of trees using the distance-augmented model (using the same optimized parameters). The model has adopted a slightly better pattern of avoiding trees, although it still has some noticeable room for improvement. Once again, there are a noticeable number of trajectories that do not make it out of the outer circle in the given number of iterations.

#### d) Experimental Setup 3

```{r,vary_tree_start,fig.width=6,echo=T}

 # modified to make a new draw and tree config
play_a_game_mod2 = function(delt,rad,theta,plt = F,trace = TRUE,nodes=c(3,3),inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
{
  J=50
  # random start
  xt=draw_starts(1) # new random start 
  objects =  objects=draw_objects(J)
  k           =   1  # Count how many iterations
  xt          =   xt # Set the initial coordinate(s) for the drone.
  trajectory = matrix(0,2,100) # store the the postions that the drone takes through out the game/how it moves
  trajectory[,1] = t(xt)

  # Check the game status:
  res_status  = game_status(xt,objects,rad)
  d_min=sqrt(sum((res_status$closest - xt)^2))

  
  if(plt)
  {
  	  plot_game(xt,objects,rad,center=matrix(c(0,0),nrow=1,ncol=2),inner_rad=0.25,outer_rad=1)
  }
  while((res_status$status==0)&(k<100)) # single game=100 steps
  {
    k = k+1
    
    # Now, let the model update the position of the pieces:
    add_arg=(1/(d_min-rad))
    ct = model_2(xt,theta,nodes,add_arg)$a2 #res_status$closest
    xt =  xt+ct*delt
    
    #print(paste0('k: ',k,'xt_new: ',xt))

    # Checkk the game status after the positions are updates:
    
    res_status  = game_status(xt,objects,rad)
    
    trajectory[,k] = t(xt)
 
  }
  trajectory = trajectory[,1:k,drop = FALSE]
    if(plt)
  {
  	lines(trajectory[2,]~trajectory[1,],col = 'darkred',lwd=2)
    #point(trajectory[2,]~trajectory[1,],col = 'darkred',lwd=2)  
    points(xt[,2]~xt[,1],pch = 9,col = 'black')
  }
  
  dmin_final=sqrt(sum((res_status$closest - xt)^2))
  
  return(list(k = k, status = res_status$status,xt= xt,trajectory = trajectory,dmin_final=dmin_final))
}
```

# Monte Carlo Tree Search

**a)**

```{r,game_tree_orig,eval=T,echo=F,include=F}
rm(list = ls())
game_tree= function(m,k)
{
	g = c()
	game_state = rho(m,S)
	if(game_state$terminal)
	{
		 g = c(g,game_state$winner)
		 return(g)
	}else{
		index = which(m == 0) # open slot on the game board/ vector of open slots
		for(i in 1:length(index))
		{
			x           = m # how the board looks before the next move
			x[index[i]] = k # next player's turn
			g           = c(g,game_tree(x,-1*k)) # recursive call, append outcome to g
		}
		return(g)
	}
}
```

```{r,game_tree_helpr_func,eval=T,echo=F,include=F}
# Define game status


#===============================================================================
# Populate the state matrix
#===============================================================================
S = matrix(0,9,8)
# Row Sums:
S[1:3,1] = 1
S[4:6,2] = 1
S[7:9,3] = 1
# Col Sums:
S[c(1,4,7),4] = 1
S[c(2,5,8),5] = 1
S[c(3,6,9),6] = 1
# Diag Sums
S[c(1,5,9),7] = 1
S[c(3,5,7),8] = 1



rho = function(m,S) 
{
  m = matrix(m,ncol = 1)
  player1  = any(t(m)%*%S == -3) # player X has won along any of the rows/col
  player2  = any(t(m)%*%S == +3) # player O has won along any of the rows/col
  m_1      = (m == -1) # player X entries on the board index /vector of booleans/ 1s an 0s
  m_2      = (m == +1) # player O entries on the board index /vector of booleans/ 1s an 0s
  tie      = sum((t(m_1)%*%S>0)*(t(m_2)%*%S>0)) == 8 # check for draw
  winner   = c(-1,0,+1,NA)[c(player1,tie,player2,NA)] # indicate what game outcome is 
  terminal = player1|tie|player2 # check if game HAS ended tie to the above conditions, returns FALSE if not
  ret      = list(terminal = terminal,winner = winner)
  return(ret)
}

```

```{r,mc_search,echo=T}


# m0 = as.matrix(c(0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0)) # current game board/flattened
# c(rho(m0,S)$winner ,1)

# Mofified game tree
game_tree_mod= function(m,k,n_moves,strict=F,n_sim=1) #n_moves=target moves
{
	g = c()
	
	for(sim in 1:n_sim){
	x=m
	game_state = rho(x,S)
	
	if(strict){
	condition=(n_moves<=0)}else{ # exactly condition
	  condition=((game_state$terminal)|(n_moves<=0)) # up to condition
	}
	
	if(condition){
		 g = c(g,game_state$winner)
		 return(g)
	}else{
		index_positions = which(m == 0) # open slot on the game board/ vector of open 

		for(i in 1:length(index_positions))
		{
		  x=m
			picked_index=index_positions[i]
			
			x[picked_index] = k # player's turn
			
			g  =c(g, game_tree_mod(x,-1*k,n_moves-1,n_sim=1) )
			
		}
		}
		return(g)
	}
	}

```

```{r,mcts,echo=T}

mcts= function(m,k,alpha,n_sim=1) 
{
	
  g = c()
	
	for(sim in 1:n_sim){
	x=m
	game_state = rho(x,S)
	
	if(game_state$terminal)
	{
		 g = c(g,game_state$winner)
		 return(g)
	}else{
		index_positions = which(m == 0) # open slot on the game board/ vector of open 

		for(i in 1:length(index_positions))
		{
		  if (runif(1,0,1) <= alpha) {
		  x=m
			picked_index=index_positions[i]
			
			x[picked_index] = k # player's turn
			g  =c(g, mcts(x,k*-1,alpha) )
			
			
		  }
		}
		}
		return(g)
	}
	}


# Table Summ

cols=c('Pl 1 Win %','Pl 2 Win %','Ties %')
alphas_=c(0.95,1)

m0=as.matrix(c(+1, +1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,0,-1))

pl_1_wins=c()
pl_2_wins=c()
ties=c()
for(alph in alphas_ ){
  if(alph!=1){
  g_sample=mcts(m0,-1,alph)
  }else{
    g_sample=game_tree(m0,-1)
  }
  
  num_traj=length(g_sample)
  num_wins_player1=round( (length(  which(g_sample==-1))/num_traj),4)
  num_wins_player2=length( which(g_sample==1))/num_traj
  num_ties=length(which(g_sample==0))/num_traj
  pl_1_wins=c(pl_1_wins,num_wins_player1)
  pl_2_wins=c(pl_2_wins,num_wins_player2)
  ties=c(ties,num_ties)
}

mcts_freq=data.frame(cbind(  round(pl_1_wins,4), round(pl_2_wins,4),round(ties,4) ))
rownames(mcts_freq)=alphas_
colnames(mcts_freq)=cols
kable( mcts_freq,
  caption="Relative Frequencies Comparison")


```

At $\alpha=0.95$, the estimated frequencies are relatively close to those of the full game tree, which is expected as alpha is fairely close to recovering the true frequencies from the whole game tree ( $\alpha=1$).

# Soft-Margin SVM

**a)**

```{r,soft_marg_svm,echo=T}

# kernal function to use the polynomial kernal trick
KK = function(X1,X2,cf,gm,dg)
 {
     return((cf+gm*t(X1)%*%X2)^dg)
}

my_svm=function(y,X,poly,Cost=10000){ # poly- vector of polynomial arguments c(gm,cf,dg)

  gm = poly[1] # coeff
  cf = poly[2] #constant
  dg = poly[3] # order of polynomial
  N=dim(X)[1]
  DD=matrix(0,N,N) 
  
  # Fill in D mat
  for(i in 1:N)
 {
     for(j in 1:N)

     {
         DD[i,j] = y[i]*y[j]*KK(X[i,],X[j,],cf=cf,gm=gm,dg=dg) # Second part of Lagragian  formulation yn*ym*zn*zm
     }
  }
   eps = 5e-6
   DD  = DD +eps*diag(N)

  # Constraints LHS
  cons_1=diag(N);dim(cons_1)#lower bound of inequlity alpha>0
  cons_2=-diag(N);dim(cons_2)#upper bound of inequality aplha< C
  const_3=matrix(y,ncol=1,nrow=N);dim(const_3) # equality constraint alpha%*%yn=0 
  Amat = cbind(const_3,cons_1,cons_2);dim(Amat) # N rows, M constraints
  d    =  matrix(1,N,1);dim(d) # coeffiencents of all alpha is 1, d in formulation 
  
  # RHS of constraints
  rhs1=rep(0,N) # lower bound
  rhs2=rep(-Cost,N)# upper bound
  rhs3=0 # equality cons
  b0=c(rhs3,rhs1,rhs2)
  bvec=b0 # RHS
  
  # Solve the opt problem
   res = solve.QP(DD, d, Amat, bvec, meq=1, factorized=FALSE)
   a   = res$solution

   # Get wieghts
    # Recover the model:

     pad.a= round(a,3)
     wh = which.max(a) #

     # Find the ws:
     ww = t(a*y)%*%X # work back the wieghts/ X be substituted by the kernel val
     intercept = 1/y[wh]-sum(a*y*KK(X[wh,],t(X),cf=cf,gm=gm, dg=dg)) # get intercept back

      T1 = rep(0,N)
      for(i in 1:N)
      {
        T1[i] = sum(a*y*KK(X[i,], t(X), cf=cf, gm=gm, dg=dg)) # matrix to get predictions/plane
      }

       yhat = sign(T1+intercept[1])

       # return list of a,weights,intercept,yhat
       ret=list(alphas=a,ww=ww,intercept=intercept,yhat=yhat)
  
      return(ret)
}


```
